Fragmentum in Proverbia
ΕΚ ΤΗΣ ΕΡΜΗΝΕΙΑΣ ΤΟΥ ΑΓΙΟΥ ΚΥΡΙΛΛΟΥ ΕΙΣ ΤΑΣ ΠΑΡΟΙΜΙΑΣ
Κύριος ἔκτισέ με. {Κυρίλλου.} Τὸ ἔκτισέ με, ἂν περὶ θεότητος ἐκλάβῃς, ἀντὶ
τοῦ Κατέστησέ με· ὡς τὸ, Καρδίαν καθαρὰν κτίσον ἐν ἐμοὶ, ὁ Θεός. Καὶ,Ἵνα τοὺς δύο
κτίσῃ ἐν ἑαυτῷ. Οὐ γὰρ οὐσιωδῶς, ἵνα κτίσῃ τοὺς ἤδη γεγενημένους, ἀλλ' ἵνα
καταστήσῃ. Κατέστησεν οὖν με ἀρχὴν τῶν προνοητικῶν αὐτοῦ καὶ ποιητικῶν
ἔργων. Καὶ τῷ ∆αβὶδ γὰρ λέγει· Ἐγὼ κατεστάθην βασιλεὺς ὑπ' αὐτοῦ.
thought_title: Created means appointed when said of the divinity
orientation: Cyril is opening his interpretation of Proverbs 8:22, explaining how the phrase 'The Lord created me' should be understood.
pass_a_gloss: Fragment on Proverbs. From the interpretation of holy Cyril on the Proverbs. The Lord created me. {Of Cyril.} The 'he created me,' if you take it about the divinity, is instead of 'he appointed me'—that is, 'he constituted me'; as the saying, 'A clean heart create in me, O God.' And, 'that he might create the two in himself.' For not as to their being, that he might create those already having come into being, but that he might appoint. Therefore Wisdom says: 'He appointed me as beginning of his works of foresight and creation.' And to David indeed he says: 'I was appointed king by him.'

choices.why: The glossary requires 'created' for κτίζω, and the pronoun must remain explicit as the object.
The glossary requires 'appointed' for καθίστημι, and this is Cyril's preferred meaning for 'created' in this context.
The glossary requires 'divinity' for θεότης, avoiding 'Godhead' and 'divine essence.'
The glossary requires 'in essence' for οὐσιωδῶς, and the negation 'not in essence' preserves Cyril's denial of essential creation.
The glossary requires 'beginning' for ἀρχή, and it fits the sense of Wisdom as the starting point of God's works.
The glossary requires 'providential' for προνοητικός, describing God's works of forethought and care.

pass_b_english: "The Lord created me" (Proverbs 8:22). If you take "he created me" as referring to the divinity, it means "he appointed me." So too: "Create a clean heart in me, O God" (Psalm 50:12 LXX; Psalm 51:12 in modern Hebrew numbering). And: "that he might create the two in himself" (Ephesians 2:15, as cited by Cyril; the standard text reads "make" and "in him"). For it is not with respect to their existence that he might create those who had already come into being, but that he might appoint them. Therefore Wisdom says: "He appointed me as the beginning of his providential and creative works." And to David he says: "I was appointed king by him" (Psalm 2:6 LXX).

problems.source_quote: Καὶ τῷ ∆αβὶδ γὰρ λέγει· Ἐγὼ κατεστάθην βασιλεὺς ὑπ' αὐτοῦ
problems.why: Source quotes David saying 'I was appointed king by him' but cites no Psalm number; this is Psalm 2:6 in some editions, but the source gives no reference. However, the brief says Psalm 50:12 and Ephesians 2:15 are cited. The David citation has no verse given in source. But more critically: the English adds '(Psalm 2:6 LXX)' where the source has no such citation. The brief does not identify this as Psalm 2:6. The source text simply says 'And to David he says: I was appointed king by him' with no Psalm reference.
problems.fix: Remove '(Psalm 2:6 LXX)' or verify if this identification is editorial.
problems.ruling: Source 'Καὶ τῷ ∆αβὶδ γὰρ λέγει' has no scripture reference; adding '(Psalm 2:6 LXX)' misrepresents the source text.
